tomato_early_blight.name: Early blight
tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Caused by Alternaria solani fungus. Starts as small dark spots with concentric bullseye rings on older lower leaves.

treatments_organic.text: Remove and burn the infected lower leaves.
Spray a neem-based solution in the evening.
Water at the base, not over the leaves.

chemical_caution.headline: A fungicide registered for tomato. Follow the label exactly.
chemical_caution.caution: Wear gloves and a mask when spraying.

cost.note: Sample pricing shown here. Subsidized rates available via Krishi Bhavan.

prevention.text: Mulch the soil around plants to prevent soil spores splashing onto lower leaves.
Maintain 45–60 cm distance between tomato plants for healthy air circulation.
Practice 3-year crop rotation; avoid planting tomatoes after potatoes or eggplants.

tomato_early_blight.fertilizer: Apply balanced organic compost; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer which softens leaf tissues.
tomato_early_blight.farmer_tip: Thoroughly destroy crop residue after harvest to break the fungal pathogen cycle for the next season.
tomato_early_blight.voice_text: Tomato leaf diagnosis: Early blight, Fungal disease. Remove infected lower leaves, spray neem solution in the evening, and water only at plant base.
tomato_early_blight.voice_treatment: Step 1: Remove and burn the infected lower leaves. Step 2: Spray a neem-based solution in the evening. Step 3: Water at the base, not over the leaves. If it keeps spreading, use a fungicide registered for tomato. Follow the label exactly and wear gloves and a mask when spraying.
tomato_early_blight.voice_prevention: Step 1: Mulch the soil around plants to prevent soil spores splashing onto lower leaves. Step 2: Maintain 45–60 cm distance between tomato plants for healthy air circulation. Step 3: Practice 3-year crop rotation; avoid planting tomatoes after potatoes or eggplants. Farmer pro tip: Thoroughly destroy crop residue after harvest to break the fungal pathogen cycle for the next season.

tomato_late_blight.name: Late blight
tomato_late_blight.symptoms: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Produces large, water-soaked pale-green to dark brown patches that spread quickly in humid weather.

treatments_organic.text: Prune severely affected stems and bury them deeply away from farm.
Apply 1% Bordeaux mixture on clear mornings on both leaf surfaces.
Ensure quick drainage and avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

chemical_caution.headline: Systemic fungicide (Metalaxyl + Mancozeb). Follow pre-harvest interval.
chemical_caution.caution: Do not harvest within 7 days of application. Wash thoroughly before consumption.

cost.note: Sample pricing shown here. Subsidized bio-fungicides available through agro clinics.

prevention.text: Use certified disease-resistant tomato varieties for rainy season planting.
Stake and trellis plants to keep leaves clean and off damp soil.
Sanitize pruning shears with spirit or bleach between plants.

tomato_late_blight.fertilizer: Avoid high potassium deficiency; maintain balanced micronutrients with calcium and boron.
tomato_late_blight.farmer_tip: Thoroughly destroy crop residue after harvest to break the fungal pathogen cycle for the next season.
tomato_late_blight.voice_text: Tomato leaf diagnosis: Late blight, Water mold disease. Prune severely affected stems, apply 1% Bordeaux mixture on clear mornings, and avoid sprinkler irrigation.
tomato_late_blight.voice_treatment: Step 1: Prune severely affected stems and bury them deeply away from farm. Step 2: Apply 1% Bordeaux mixture on clear mornings on both leaf surfaces. Step 3: Ensure quick drainage and avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation. If it keeps spreading, use systemic fungicide Metalaxyl + Mancozeb. Do not harvest within 7 days of application.
tomato_late_blight.voice_prevention: Step 1: Use certified disease-resistant tomato varieties for rainy season planting. Step 2: Stake and trellis plants to keep leaves clean and off damp soil. Step 3: Sanitize pruning shears with spirit or bleach between plants. Farmer pro tip: Thoroughly destroy crop residue after harvest to break the fungal pathogen cycle for the next season.

tomato_healthy.name: Healthy leaf
tomato_healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green foliage with no detectable fungal lesions, blight, or severe pest damage.

treatments_organic.text: No disease treatment required. Continue regular maintenance.
Apply organic compost or vermicompost every 3 weeks at plant base.
Inspect the undersides of leaves weekly for early signs of whiteflies or aphids.

chemical_caution.headline: No chemicals recommended.
chemical_caution.caution: Keep chemical sprays away from healthy crops to protect beneficial pollinators.

cost.note: Preventive maintenance saves up to 40% of seasonal plant protection costs.

prevention.text: Spray mild diluted cow urine or Panchagavya monthly to boost natural immunity.
Install yellow sticky traps to catch flying sucking pests early.
Keep field perimeter free of wild solanaceous weeds.

tomato_healthy.fertilizer: Continue applying vermicompost and fermented bio-fertilizers like Jeevamrutha every 2–3 weeks.
tomato_healthy.farmer_tip: Regular inspection in early morning helps spot any pest or fungus before it establishes.
tomato_healthy.voice_text: Tomato leaf diagnosis: Healthy crop. No disease detected. Continue regular organic maintenance and water at base.
tomato_healthy.voice_treatment: No disease treatment required. Continue regular maintenance. Step 2: Apply organic compost or vermicompost every 3 weeks at plant base. Step 3: Inspect the undersides of leaves weekly for early signs of whiteflies or aphids. No chemicals recommended.
